newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fragile Australian dlr survives first crucial test.
newsitem.headline: Fragile Australian dlr survives first crucial test.

text.p: The Australian dollar survived a first brush with pivotal support Tuesday but the rally lacked the vim needed to suggest its two week-old slide was over.

It came uncomfortably close to its year low of US$0.7550 offshore as the market wondered if the Reserve Bank might surprise yet again by opening its monthly meeting today with an immediate rate cut. In the event silence ruled and a short covering rally ensued, encouraged by a chunky AUD/yen buy order.
The resilience of support was balm for bulls made desperate by its recent two cent fall, but offshore sellers showed no sign of giving up either and offers were thick around US$0.7610.
By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the local currency had crept up to US$0.7595/00 from an early US$0.7572/77 and Monday's late US$0.7580/85, but was short of the US$0.7610 top hit offshore.

Dealers, most of whom admit to being bearish on the currency, were frankly surprised by the depth of support at US$0.7550. This level marks the low for the year so far, reached in early February, and is viewed as a major chart bulwark.

"Those holding short positions may become uncomfortable if this holds for a couple more days," said one, adding there could yet be a bounce back to US$0.7680 -- the level held before Friday's dire retail sales data stoked talk of another rate cut.

Indeed, such is the market's uncertainty over the direction of policy in the wake of the surprise easing on May 23 that some feared the RBA might even open today's monthly board meeting with the announcement of a cut.

Analysts noted it would be extremely unusual for the bank to move twice in such a short time and expected it to absorb at least another month of data before deciding if further insurance was warranted.
That would not stop the market from tensing for Wednesday morning's RBA operation, or later in the week if the March quarter GDP data out tomorrow were as weak as some expect.

These are somewhat dated now but still provide a comprehensive outline of the economy as it stood in the first quarter, including data on labours costs, productivity and inflation which will go into the interest rate equation.

Median forecasts are for a quarterly rise of 0.8 percent which would still see annual growth slow sharply to 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent in Q4. However, estimates range as low as 0.25 percent which would give yr-yr growth of just 1.75 percent.
Anything like the latter would stoke speculation another easing lay in wait and see market rates ease further.

Analysts, as analysts do, are already refining the timing of any possible move and many argue the bank will at least wait to see whether the Federal Reserve meeting on July 1-2 decides to tighten U.S. policy.
It was common knowledge that prior to the last easing the RBA was sounding out the major banks for their opinion on how the Australian dollar would fare if domestic rates fell below those in the U.S.
On the crosses the local dollar seesawed on the yen as an early buy order lifted it 1/2 yen to 88.80 only for the gains to be wiped out by a retreat in US$/yen.
It ended at 88.18/28 yen from 88.20/30 late Monday.
Dealers said the U.S. dollar was upset by rumours, later denied, that Finance Ministry forex guru Eisuke Sakakibara had mentioned 103 yen as a suitable level for the dollar.
But both dollars took comfort in comments from the MOF and Bank of Japan that the present low settings of Japanese interest rates were necessary to ensure economic recovery.
The Canadian dollar whipsawed as the results from the general election there flowed one way then another.
It dived at first as early results suggested the ruling Liberal Party might actually be defeated.
But it recouped the losses when it became clear it would win with a majority, albeit a much reduced one.
Analysts saw potential for division longer term, however, given three opposition parties representing different regions of Canada were returned with sizeable blocks of seats.

The Canadian dollar thus ended only a shade firmer on the day at C$1.3758/63 after ranging as low as C$1.3830 and as high as C$1.3717. The A$ was firmer on the day at C$1.0451/61 after recovering from an early C$1.0405 low.
In trade weighted terms it was up a shade at 57.9 from 57.8 late Monday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
